claims.text: Adding 2–5 vol% uniformly dispersed WC nanoparticles to the high-entropy-alloy intermediate layer will improve its effective heat-transfer capability.
The WC-modified layer will retain structural integrity under plasma-facing reactor conditions.
A powder-metallurgy consolidation route can produce a uniform dispersion of 2–5 vol% WC nanoparticles in the alloy.
The proposed behavior will hold at approximately 500–800°C under cyclic mechanical loading typical of reactor conditions.
Dispersed WC nanoparticles will form continuous heat-transfer pathways through the alloy matrix.
The WC nanoparticle dispersion will strengthen the bulk alloy.
WC nanoparticles have sufficiently high intrinsic thermal conductivity to provide additional heat-conduction pathways in this matrix.
WC nanoparticles hinder dislocation motion in the high-entropy-alloy matrix.
Hindering dislocation motion will preserve the alloy's mechanical strength.
Uniform nanoparticle dispersion will prevent stress concentrations that could degrade structural performance.
The modified alloy will have approximately 20–30% higher effective thermal conductivity than the unmodified intermediate layer under the tested conditions.
The modified alloy will maintain yield strength similar to that of the unmodified intermediate layer.
The modified alloy will maintain fracture toughness similar to that of the unmodified intermediate layer.
The expected enhancement requires a uniform WC distribution and a WC fraction not exceeding roughly 5 vol%.
Excessive WC addition may cause nanoparticle agglomeration.
Agglomeration or excessive WC addition may cause embrittlement and compromise mechanical properties.
